svg.text: K4b LOOP + NOSE — the arm holds the free end of the mat: it rolls food, or lays it down
LOOP: the arm pays out a loop and runs with E — slices roll up in it. NOSE: the arm moves the hem along while winding.
loop ≈ 1.1 × roll circumference (≈ 160 mm) · 2 turns
camera stops the seam at 5 o’clock
sheets ≤ 380 × 280 laid flat, no stretching
mat tension 25 N (dancer) · bar Ø 40, hem key slot
A LOOP: rolling a Roulade (E and the bar run together)
table
E
G
comb cradle on P1
loop

text.tspan: E feeds the filled slice (sides folded by plough rails)
into the loop; E and bar run together: it rolls 2 turns
the camera sees the seam and stops the mat
the bar winds on: the roll drops 40 mm into a cradle

svg.text: Same loop also rolls wraps, sponge roll and Maultaschen; as a pocket it catches cut food.
Then a hairpin raft fork through the cradle holds four rolls for searing and braising.
Untested: the first turn on wet silicone (fallback: steel pins through the cradle slots).
B NOSE: laying a dough sheet flat onto a tray (retracting nose)
table
E
anvil stick lifted out first
tray (on P3)
bar moves along X at mat speed

text.tspan: the sheet (dough 380 × 280 × 4 mm) rides on mat D over E
at the bar the arm moves along the tray while winding: laid flat, not stretched

svg.text: Same move lays cutlets onto a rack, patties into a pan, spaghetti end-first into a basket,
three shingled slices onto a plate on P1, a log into a loaf tin.
Mat at ≤ 25° from the top of E straight to the bar.

g.text: 1/2 Both moves use only E (one servo) and the arm holding the hem — no extra mechanism
2/2 The loop rolls food; the moving, winding bar delivers it — like a conveyor whose nose can travel
